evidence.reason: At line 619 the publication push is unconditional: the code only checks the PR head at line 607, then pushes without a lease. If the remote branch is reset from the checked head B to ancestor A in that window, the prepared commit C remains a fast-forward from A, so the push succeeds and restores the removed B commits. The recovery push at line 651 has the same race. Requiring the remote branch still equal the checked SHA (for example a force-with-lease-style condition) is a concrete correctness fix, not a new requirement.
